In Figure A, L1 and L2 are connected successively on the same wire, and the whole is connected between the two ends marked with voltage U, so the two lamps are in series. In Figure B, the left and right sides are the same pair of nodes, L1 is on the upper branch, L2 is on the middle branch, and both branches are connected across the same pair of nodes; voltage U is applied to this pair of nodes, so the two lamps are in parallel, and L1 is directly connected to the two ends of voltage U.
Then reason: The brightness of a bulb is determined by its actual power. When Figure A is in series, the total voltage is U, and L2 can also emit light, which shows that L2 gets a part of the voltage, so the voltage across L1 is less than U; when Figure B is in parallel, the voltage across L1 is U. For the same lamp L1, the greater the voltage across it, the greater the actual power, and the brighter the lamp. Therefore, L1 in Figure B is brighter than L1 in Figure A.
